chapter: Family band and learning to play
title: Touring Oklahoma and Kansas City; tenor player Milton Thomas
summary: The band grows popular, travels in touring cars, and Milton Thomas, a tenor player who made money in trucks, influences Tate to take up tenor.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So after the band started, we started playing -- the band became so popular and we started playing other towns, like in Oklahoma and all around, you know. We'd go as far as Oklahoma City and we went to Kansas City a couple of times. We thought that was really it then, you know, we thought we really had it made.
Well, we had -- in cars, touring cars, you know, we had two touring cars we used to travel --
How many guys in the band?
Well, now, by this time, we had six. We had the tenor player that really was my -- that influenced me to want to play tenor. His name was Milton Thomas, Nobody ever knew him. He had had a --
Was he the guy who started the trucks?
That's with the trucks, yeah, yeah. That's where he made his money, he got rich with trucks, you know.
He's got a lot of money now. But he still plays. He's playing with a white band now. He told me he's 75 years old. I didn't know he was that --
He's in Dallas. He lived in Dallas then, but we used to bring him up there and he would stay with us

because we had a lot of gigs and -- you know, he was making money and we brought him up there. He couldn't read. Had a beautiful sound on tenor and of course, like when he left, he left, then I started playing tenor, when he left.
